stories.h: Trump says he urged Putin to end aggression in Europe
stories.p: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to pull back all military aggression in Europe. Punch notes the remark marks a change in tone, coming a week after Trump described the Russian leader as his friend during a visit to China.

stories.h: Prisons hold over 4,000 inmates on death row
stories.p: The Nigerian Correctional Service says more than 4,000 inmates are on death row and that custodial centres across the country are badly congested. The service urged state governors either to commute the death sentences to life imprisonment or to sign the execution warrants, Channels Television reported on Thursday.

stories.h: APC says Tinubu housing schemes built 26,000 homes
stories.p: Housing programmes under President Bola Tinubu have delivered 26,000 units through the Housing Ministry, the Federal Housing Authority and the Federal Mortgage Bank, the APC said on Thursday. Party spokesman Alake added that the schemes created 525,100 construction jobs in three years and that new mortgage measures aim to draw private investment.

stories.h: Navy destroys four illegal refineries in Rivers
stories.p: The Nigerian Navy says it dismantled four illegal refining sites in Rivers State and found about 112,525 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and illegally refined diesel in separate operations. Navy spokesman Captain Abiodun Folorunsho announced the results on Thursday, saying oil thieves keep trying to restart such sites.

stories.h: Free trade zone status for Anambra Industrial City
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has approved free trade zone status for Anambra Industrial City and has also approved two flyovers in Awka, Vice President Kashim Shettima said on Thursday. Shettima made the announcement while inaugurating a newly built flyover at Ekwulobia in Anambra State, Punch reports.

stories.h: NGX ends losing streak as stocks gain N61bn
stories.p: Nigerian stocks rose on Thursday, ending a run of losing sessions on the Nigerian Exchange as investors bought heavyweight energy, banking and financial services shares. Nigerian Tribune put the market's gain at about N61 billion, while the All-Share Index edged up 0.04 per cent, according to Leadership.

stories.h: INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units Saturday
stories.p: INEC will hold a mock test of its voter accreditation technology, the BVAS, in Ondo State on Saturday, November 28, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise runs from 8:30am to 2:30pm in 406 polling units across all 18 local government areas of the state, the commission said.

stories.h: Burkina Faso asks Nigeria for help against terrorism
stories.p: Burkina Faso's Security Minister Mahamadou Sana has called for closer security cooperation with Nigeria against terrorism, drug and human trafficking and other cross-border crimes in West Africa. He made the request in Ouagadougou while meeting Nigeria's ambassador, Syndoph Endoni, and cited the Dangote Refinery as an example of Nigeria's industrial progress.

stories.h: Osun NSCDC deploys 1,300 for Adeleke inauguration
stories.p: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Osun State has deployed 1,300 personnel across the state for Governor Ademola Adeleke's second-term inauguration on Friday, November 27. Command spokesperson Adeleke Kehinde said the deployment is meant to protect lives and property and ensure a peaceful ceremony.

stories.h: FG reports 17% drop in maternal deaths in 172 LGAs
stories.p: The Federal Government says maternal deaths have fallen by 17 per cent and newborn deaths by four per cent in 172 local government areas it classes as high-risk for mothers and babies, Nigerian Tribune reported on Thursday. The figures were presented as results of federal maternal and child health interventions in those areas.

stories.h: Ogun police recover baby taken at Ifo market
stories.p: Ogun State Police Command says it has rescued a one-year-old boy who was allegedly snatched from his mother at Ifo Market in August and later sold. Detectives found him in Abeokuta with a couple who reportedly believed they were adopting through a Lagos orphanage. Three female suspects were arrested and the child was reunited with his mother.

stories.h: Aubameyang unhurt after car crash in Spain
stories.p: Gabon striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was not hurt when his Ferrari collided with another car on Spain's AP-9 motorway on Thursday morning while he was driving to Deportivo La Coruña training. He said on Instagram the other driver was fine, and he still trained ahead of this weekend's LaLiga match against Barcelona.

stories.h: NAFDAC shuts Zuba market, seizes N300m fake goods
stories.p: NAFDAC has shut Zuba International Market in the FCT after an enforcement raid in which more than 160 shops were screened and counterfeit and unwholesome products worth over N300 million were seized. The agency said Director-General Mojisola Adeyeye ordered the crackdown to protect consumers from fake goods during the yuletide season.

stories.h: Tinubu gives NAF crash families homes, N100m
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has approved three-bedroom flats in Abuja and N100 million for the families of the 25 people killed in the Nigerian Air Force ATR 42 crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State. He announced the support on Thursday at a memorial and wreath-laying with service chiefs at the National Cemetery in Abuja, Punch reports.

stories.h: Lawal again rules out talks with Zamfara bandits
stories.p: Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal said on Thursday his government will not negotiate with bandits or their sponsors and will focus on retaking ungoverned areas. He spoke in Gusau at the graduation of 1,000 Zamfara Forest Guards, an armed forest guard scheme launched by President Tinubu in May 2025.

stories.h: CBN lifts BDC weekly dollar cash limit to $1m
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has temporarily raised the amount of dollar cash licensed Bureau De Change operators can buy each week from $150,000 to $1 million. The change took effect on Wednesday, 25 November, and is meant to ease seasonal demand for foreign currency as the naira weakened past N1,400 per dollar, Business Post reports.

stories.h: LAMATA adds 24 coaches to Lagos Red Line
stories.p: The Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority says three new train sets with a total of 24 coaches will be put on the Lagos Red Line rail. The agency says the extra trains should allow more frequent services and reduce the disruptions commuters have faced on the route, Punch reports.

stories.h: Court orders arrest of Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
stories.p: A Lagos State High Court in Ikoyi on Thursday issued a bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya after he failed to appear in contempt proceedings brought by the trustees of the Fountain of Life Church. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin also sent the case back to the administrative judge for reassignment.

stories.h: FG vows to protect voters and INEC staff in 2027
stories.p: National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu said the Federal Government will protect voters, politicians, parties and INEC officials before, during and after the 2027 general election. At a meeting of INEC and security agencies on Thursday, INEC chairman Joash Amupitan warned parties that violence, intimidation and the use of thugs could keep voters away.

stories.h: NNPC stations cut petrol price to N1,240
stories.p: NNPC Limited filling stations have reduced the pump price of petrol by N60, from N1,300 to N1,240 per litre, according to a Daily Post market survey on Thursday. It is another cut by NNPC retail outlets, and comes as the Dangote refinery lowered its diesel gantry price to N1,595 per litre this week.

stories.h: Electricity metering rate rises to 64.69%
stories.p: Distribution companies metered 144,694 more customers in October 2026, lifting Nigeria's national electricity metering rate to 64.69 per cent from 63.99 per cent in September. The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission gave the figures in its latest metering factsheet released on Thursday, TVC News reports.

stories.h: FFS starts harmattan fire safety campaign
stories.p: The Federal Fire Service has flagged off its harmattan safety campaign and urged Nigerians not to overload electrical sockets, leave cooking unattended, burn refuse carelessly or store petrol at home. The Federal Government also warned against attacks on firefighters during emergencies, Vanguard reports from Abuja.

stories.h: Six die as bus catches fire on Badagry Expressway
stories.p: Six people died and 12 were injured when a commercial bus caught fire at Magbon on the Lagos-Badagry Expressway on Thursday morning, the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service said. The service received the distress call at 8:44am and linked the blaze to extra fuel carried in the vehicle. One outlet put the death toll at eight.

stories.h: Court refuses to quash Saleh Mamman's N31bn charge
stories.p: Justice Maryanne Anenih of the FCT High Court on Thursday dismissed an application by former Power Minister Saleh Mamman to quash a nine-count fraud and forgery charge filed by the EFCC. The case concerns N31.07 billion allegedly diverted from funds for the Mambilla and Zungeru hydropower projects. His trial will now continue.

stories.h: FIFA confirms hackers stole personal, business data
stories.p: FIFA has confirmed a criminal cyberattack that gave hackers access to a limited amount of personal and business information. A group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club has claimed responsibility and says it took about 12GB of data. FIFA said files on its dropped World Cup stake-sale plan were not accessed.

stories.h: Super Falcons to play Algeria twice from Nov 30
stories.p: Coach Augustine Eguavoen has named his Super Falcons squad for two friendlies against Algeria, on 30 November and 4 December. The first match is at the 5 July 1962 Stadium in Algiers at 6pm Nigerian time. The games are preparation for the third round of 2028 Olympic qualifiers against Morocco.

stories.h: Gunmen kill at least 16 in Plateau village attack
stories.p: At least 16 people, including women and children, were killed when gunmen attacked Tafi Gana near Jebbu Miango in Bassa LGA, Plateau State, at about 11:30pm on Wednesday, the Irigwe Development Association said. Four people were injured. Vanguard later reported the toll had risen to 19 after three injured people died in hospital.

stories.h: NPA cargo up 12.2% to 68.2m tonnes in H1
stories.p: The Nigerian Ports Authority handled 68.2 million metric tonnes of cargo in the first half of 2026, a 12.2 per cent rise, Business Post reports. In 2025, cargo throughput at Nigerian ports grew 24.8 per cent, from 103.6 million to 129.3 million tonnes, according to NPA figures.

stories.h: FCT activates cholera emergency centre
stories.p: The Federal Capital Territory Administration has activated its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre to contain the cholera outbreak in Abuja. Officials say the move is meant to stop the disease from spreading as crowds and travel increase ahead of the Christmas and New Year celebrations, Punch reports.

stories.h: Dangote cuts diesel gantry price to N1,595
stories.p: Dangote Petroleum Refinery has lowered the gantry price of diesel by N125 per litre, from N1,720 to N1,595, from Thursday, November 26. The 7.27 per cent cut should reduce costs for petroleum marketers and bulk buyers who lift diesel (AGO) directly from the refinery, TVC News reports.

stories.h: Obi mourns Pete Edochie as great loss to Africa
stories.p: NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi has paid tribute to veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie, calling his death a deep loss to his hometown Nteje, the Igbo people, Nigeria and Africa. In a post on X on Wednesday, Obi praised the actor's famous role in Things Fall Apart and his contribution to African culture.

stories.h: Naira firms to N1,392 per dollar
stories.p: The naira gained N1.87, or 0.13 per cent, against the US dollar in the official NAFEM market on Wednesday, November 25, closing at N1,392.25/$1 from N1,394.12/$1 on Tuesday. The currency also rose by N5.38 against the British pound in the official market, Business Post reports.

stories.h: Oshoala earns master's in sports management
stories.p: Super Falcons forward Asisat Oshoala, 32, has graduated with a Master of Science degree in International Sports Management from the Global Institute of Sport. She attended the convocation at Wembley Stadium in London. Premium Times notes the degree could prepare her for a later move into sports administration.

stories.h: Niger gives N148m to families after Borgu killings
stories.p: Niger State Governor Mohammed Bago has ordered an investigation into the communal violence in Borgu and announced N2 million for the family of each of the 74 people killed, N148 million in total, Premium Times reports. The police have already sent a Deputy Inspector-General to the area.

stories.h: Katsina panel to probe Emir of Daura allegations
stories.p: The Katsina State Government has set up a judicial panel to investigate alleged misconduct involving the Emir of Daura. The panel is to examine the allegations, hear from everyone involved and submit its findings and recommendations to the state government within four weeks, Channels TV reports.

stories.h: Spectranet to shut service in Ibadan, Port Harcourt
stories.p: Internet provider Spectranet says it will end its broadband services in Ibadan and Port Harcourt in six months, citing rising operating challenges. The company has told customers how device buybacks and unused data will be handled, and set out its plans for Lagos and Abuja, where it continues to operate.

stories.h: Dangote refinery shares to trade on NGX Dec 1
stories.p: Shares of Dangote Petroleum Refinery will start trading on the Nigerian Exchange on December 1, Dangote Group vice-president for oil and gas Devakumar Edwin said on Wednesday, according to Reuters. The listing follows the refinery's initial public offering, which drew strong interest from investors.

stories.h: DR Congo's Tshisekedi urges end to raw mineral exports
stories.p: DR Congo President Felix Tshisekedi has called on African countries to process more of their minerals at home instead of exporting them raw. Opening the Makutano Mining 2026 Forum in Kinshasa, he urged stronger regional industrial partnerships so Africans keep more of the economic gains from their resources.

stories.h: No party names on mock accreditation ballots
stories.p: INEC says ballot papers for Saturday's nationwide mock accreditation will not carry the names of any registered political party. Chairman Joash Amupitan said that under a strengthened IReV process, polling unit results on Form EC8A will pass automatic arithmetic and over-voting checks before upload.

stories.h: Nigeria's Ogunsakin reaches J500 quarter-final
stories.p: Nigerian junior tennis player Seun Ogunsakin beat world junior No. 17 Tanishk Konduri of the United States 7-5, 6-4 on Wednesday in the third round of the J500 event in Merida, Mexico. It is his first quarter-final at a J500 tournament and the biggest win of his junior career.

stories.h: Troops rescue five kidnap victims in Kaduna
stories.p: Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma rescued five kidnapped people, including a woman and a baby, after suspected terrorists attacked Dan Bushiya community in Chikun LGA, Kaduna State, on Wednesday, army spokesman Sinivie said. The Sun reports two suspects were arrested in separate operations.

stories.h: INEC chairman says he receives threats daily
stories.p: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan says he receives threats every day over his work as the commission prepares for the 2027 general election, BusinessDay reports. His remarks come as INEC finalises the voter register of about 100 million and readies a nationwide mock accreditation exercise.

stories.h: INEC says registered voters now about 100 million
stories.p: INEC chairman Professor Joash Amupitan says Nigeria's voter register now stands at about 100 million after duplicate entries, such as one person with several registrations, were removed. With about 50 days left before the 2027 general election, he told resident electoral commissioners there is no room for errors and urged neutrality.

stories.h: Appeal court convicts Omokore in $823m oil case
stories.p: The Court of Appeal has set aside businessman Jide Omokore's acquittal and convicted him in the $823m oil fraud case, Premium Times reported on Thursday. The ruling followed an appeal by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) against the earlier judgment of the Federal High Court, which had freed him.

stories.h: IGP suspends 'wanted' notice on Obaigbena, others
stories.p: Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu on Wednesday night overruled a decision by AIG Jimoh to declare THISDAY publisher Nduka Obaigbena, the Nestoil chairman, a Sahara Group executive director and others wanted. Police spokesman Ani said the declaration is set aside pending the investigation, and the case moves to the Force Intelligence Department.

stories.h: Makinde, Atiku camps query Tinubu's budget cut
stories.p: The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation questioned President Tinubu's N3.1tn cut to 2026 spending, asking why the N31.4tn deficit and borrowing plan were kept. The Sun reports ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar also asked the government to explain a N10.78tn oil revenue shortfall. The Presidency's reply was not reported.

stories.h: Nigeria offers Poland 65 projects worth $78.5bn
stories.p: Finance minister Taiwo Oyedele has invited Polish investors to fund 65 ready projects worth about $78.5 billion, which he said could create 366,000 jobs. ThisDay reports that Poland has committed over $150 million to the Lagos ports upgrade and pledged more than $500 million in credit guarantees.

stories.h: Sanwo-Olu opens 5km Ijegun-Ijagemo road
stories.p: Lagos Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu on Wednesday commissioned the 5km Ijegun/Ijagemo Road in Alimosho Local Government Area of the state, ThisDay reported. Speaking at the event, the governor said his administration had kept the promises it made to Lagos residents and would continue to deliver projects.

stories.h: Reps approve $28.2bn, €1.04bn foreign loans
stories.p: The House of Representatives has approved President Bola Tinubu's request for external borrowing of about $28.23 billion and €1.05 billion. ThisDay reports the loans are meant to finance critical infrastructure and other development projects across the country. The request was sent to the National Assembly earlier by the President.

stories.h: 364-day treasury bill rate rises to 16.60%
stories.p: The stop rate on Nigeria's 364-day treasury bill rose by 0.71 percentage points to 16.60% at Wednesday's primary market auction, Business Post reports. The N100bn offer drew bids worth N794.17bn, almost eight times the amount on sale, and N625.09bn was allotted to investors at the close.

stories.h: FG spent N4.17tn on capital projects in H1 2026
stories.p: The federal government spent about N4.18tn on capital projects in the first half of 2026, according to a Budget Office report cited by Punch. The report shows ministries, departments and agencies received no capital releases under the 2026 budget, leaving a 74.12% shortfall against the plan for the period.

stories.h: NPERA starts new law to cut port charges
stories.p: The Nigerian Port Economic Regulatory Agency (NPERA) has begun putting its new enabling law into effect to tackle high port charges and poor services, Director-General Dr Pius Akutah said at a strategy programme in Lagos. He said the agency also aims to fund itself through its own revenue.

stories.h: Fuel tanker fire kills at least 30 in Cairo
stories.p: At least 30 people died in Cairo on Wednesday evening after a fuel tanker overturned on a busy ring road and caught fire, Egypt's health ministry said, according to AFP. Legit.ng put the toll at 31 dead and 21 injured. Video verified by AFP showed a huge blaze in the crowded city.

stories.h: Niger governor gets report on 37 miners' deaths
stories.p: Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago has received the report of the judicial commission of inquiry into the deaths of 37 artisanal miners held in Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps custody. The commission said 41 people testified at its public hearing. The report's findings have not yet been made public.

stories.h: Man United draw at Sporting; Lille beat Bayern
stories.p: Bruno Fernandes scored twice in the second half but Manchester United drew 2-2 at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, so Mauricio Pochettino is still waiting for his first win as coach. A goalkeeping error by Senne Lammens let Sporting level. Elsewhere, Lille stunned Bayern Munich 2-1.

stories.h: Naira gains against dollar for first time in days
stories.p: The naira strengthened to N1,392.25 per dollar on the official market on Wednesday, from N1,394.12 on Monday, Central Bank of Nigeria data cited by Daily Post show. The N1.87 gain ended a run of daily losses, a day after the currency closed at its weakest level in nearly nine months.

stories.h: Adeleke dissolves Osun cabinet before inauguration
stories.p: Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke dissolved the State Executive Council on Wednesday ahead of his second-term inauguration, while keeping the Secretary to the State Government and some other officials. He said his government had delivered in education, health, infrastructure, digital economy and other areas over the past four years.

stories.h: Senator's aide hurt in National Assembly clash
stories.p: National Assembly management has opened an investigation after Kingsley Wali, an aide to Senator Allwell Onyesoh (Rivers East), was injured in Abuja on Wednesday. Vanguard reported he was allegedly assaulted by security operatives attached to the Senate Appropriations Committee, chaired by Senator Olamilekan Adeola, and suffered head injuries.

stories.h: Madagascar parliament elects new speaker
stories.p: Madagascar's National Assembly has elected Marco Tsaradia as its new speaker with 129 of 130 votes, Punch reported on Wednesday. The vote followed the surprise removal of the previous speaker, Siteny Randrianasoloniaiko, by lawmakers. The Indian Ocean island nation lies off the south-east coast of Africa.

stories.h: US embassy, Lagos consulate shut Nov 26–27
stories.p: The United States Embassy in Abuja and its consulate in Lagos will be closed on Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, for the American Thanksgiving holiday, Punch reported on Wednesday. Consular services will be affected on both days, so anyone with a planned visit should check their appointment.
